received: Last week our class received a shiny trophy for tidy work.
She smiled because she received a birthday card from every friend.
We received lots of kind messages after the school play last night!
receive: The winner will stand on the stage to receive the shiny cup.
What present would you like to receive on your birthday?
Our class will receive a new book box from the library on Monday.
receipt: The cashier printed a long receipt after I paid for the biscuits.
If the toaster breaks, bring it back with the receipt!
Where did I put the receipt for my new trainers?
receiver: Gran held the receiver to her ear to hear the voice.
Put the receiver back on the phone when you finish talking.
The old phone had a long curly wire joined to its receiver.
deceive: It is wrong to deceive your friends with a made-up story.
The magician wanted to deceive us by hiding the coin in his sleeve.
Don't let the tricky puzzle deceive you, because the answer is simple.
deceit: Telling lies to win the game was an act of deceit.
Honesty is the opposite of deceit, so always tell the truth.
There was no deceit in her smile, and she meant every kind word.
conceited: Don't be conceited just because you won the sack race.
The conceited peacock kept showing off and saying he was the best bird.
A conceited rooster crowed loudly, sure that the sun rose just for him.
deceitful: It was deceitful to say you had finished when you had not.
The deceitful shopkeeper said the old bike was brand new.
What a deceitful thing to copy my picture and say it was yours!
perceive: Through the foggy window I could just perceive the shape of the bus.
Do you perceive a difference between the two shades of blue paint?
Bats can perceive tiny sounds that people cannot hear.
conceive: Try to conceive a new game we can play at break time.
She sat with her sketchbook to conceive a poster for the fair.
Who could conceive such a lovely design for a paper boat?
